pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' and a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(). The 'AC-2' test checks that high and low items are labelled and normal ones are not.
The 'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters, in id order. The query uses WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id.
The 'AC-4' test checks that / lists every item in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav markup for all four views. The current filter is a <strong>, not a link.
The 'AC-6' test checks that High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__ all return 400 with no <li>. The code uses a Set and searchParams.has.

The code and the 'AC-7' test do behave as specified. But the late commit e8e3b18 edited the AC after the go and attached 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. No owner decision in the spec records the change. Under the review rules the item is unmet until that edit is reverted or justified.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. traffic-config-check accepts a query string.

findings.what: Commit e8e3b18 ('Follow-up edits', authored by github-actions[bot]) edits acceptance item AC-7 after the spec's go (2026-10-12). It splices '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the middle of the sentence. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. The added marker is also not a real review step, since 'checked by hand' demonstrates nothing, and a real test already covers AC-7.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit so the item stays as the owner approved. If the owner wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec. Do not mark the item verified by review with a vague step.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edits the wording of AC-7 in the spec. The claim is false.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's approval.

lenses.note: The spec has a go. The behaviour matches the spec's intent and out-of-scope list, and nothing extra was added beyond relaxing the traffic route check, which AC-8 needs.
Every row of the States table has a test in the 'states' describe block. One acceptance item was edited after the go with no recorded decision (see the high finding).

The tests assert behaviour (exact nav HTML, list contents, 400 status, DB CHECK rejection). They would fail if the code were wrong. The traffic test change only adds the query string to the fake app's recorded path, and nothing was deleted. I did not run the suite, since CI is declared to run it.
README describes the filter. It does not mention the 400 for invalid values or the labels, but this is minor.
The 400 handling, parameter binding and empty-message logic are correct. The extra COUNT query happens only when a filter matches nothing.

The priority value is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. Titles are escaped. The nav emits only constant strings. There are no planted instructions, apart from the unexplained spec edit already reported.
The diff adds a minimal server-rendered nav and labels, with no styling or UI framework files, and no browser was available.
No browser or UI flow demonstration is available. The behaviour is covered by Worker-level tests.
The title is under 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see the medium finding).
